text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Planning Minister Joao Cravinho says the construction of Lisbon's new international airport is directly linked to Airport Authority ANA's privatisation. Whoever keeps the concession will be responsible for the construction of the airport.
- Portuguese state airline TAP negotiated a 6.5 percent interest rate with French banks financing its Airbus purchases.

- Popular Party (PP) 1997 budget proposals presented yesterday to the Government will cost, but the deficit will remain inside the 2.9 percent objective, the paper quotes a government source as saying.
- Unemployment and salary restrictions may prevent significant revival in private consumption until the end of 1997, says a report from the Economy Ministry published in today's paper.
- Banif Bank is interested in a partnership with Portugal's CTT to create a postal bank, Banif chairman Castro Rocha told the paper.
- Trades unions accuse the Governement of political incoherence and refuse to accept 2.6 percent salary rises for 1997.
- Philips inaugurates on Friday a factory to produce parts for mobile phones, faxes and monitors. Investment will be over four billion escudos and it will create 600 jobs.
- Government and state airline TAP ponder what to do about Lisbon-Macau link which lost two billion escudos in first year.
